item.title: Monaghan Lions Club launch annual hamper appeal
item.description: Members of the Monaghan Lions Club are coming together this weekend to collect for their annual Christmas food hamper appeal. The group will collect on Friday from 5pm to 9pm, Saturday from 11am to 7pm and on Sunday from 2pm to 6pm. This year's collection points are, Fleming's Supervalu and Monaghan Shopping Centre and at Church Square. item.title: Gardai issue direct appeal over fatal Monaghan Town collision
item.description: Gardai in Monaghan town investigating a fatal road traffic collision at Old Cross Square that occurred last Saturday, are seeking assistance in identifying witnesses. They are issuing an appeal for anyone who witnessed the incident and have not yet come forward. Shortly after 10:15am last Saturday, Gardaí and emergency services were alerted to the collision, involving a lorry and a pedestrian. item.title: Annual Christmas Lights Vehicle Parade set to take place
item.description: The Christmas Lights Vehicle Parade is back for 2025 and it's even bigger and better. The event has been renamed in honour of their friend and colleague, Kevin Smith. The annual charity event has raised over €365,000 for local charities since its inception. item.title: One of Monaghan’s finest land holding makes €30,000 per acre
item.description: One of Co. Monaghan’s Finest Land Holdings that was on the market has achieved €30,000 per acre. Fee & Associates based in Cootehill say they are pleased to announce the successful sale of Annareagh House and its c.60 acres of prime agricultural land at Annareagh South, Glaslough, which achieved a record price of €1.8 million. Recognised as one of the most significant land holdings to come to market in Co. Monaghan in 2025, the property drew substantial interest from across the region and beyond

item.title: New anti-racism project targeting the region to be launched
item.description: Members of the public are being invited to the official launch of an exciting new project aimed at building positive relationships in communities experiencing rapid demographic change. The Intercultural Cross-border Inclusion Programme, supported by PEACEPLUS, has been developed by an alliance of five grassroots organisations. item.title: New boat gifted to Meath River Rescue
item.description: Meath River Rescue who had spent over a month on searches for two missing people in Navan has been gifted a new boat. Members say they were left gobsmacked when fundraising efforts to afford a 62,000 euro boat were answered in full. On an online post the group says they had amassed over €13,000 on their iDonate page as a result of kind donations from local businesses and people in recognition of their work. item.title: N2 remains closed until 9pm tonight following fatal collision
item.description: A man remains in custody following a fatal collision in Co Monaghan. The man aged in his 50 arrested remains detained in Garda custody under section 4 of the Criminal Justice Act, 1984. Gardai say the N2 remains closed as forensic investigations continue at the scene and diversions remain in place. Advertisement The N2 will remain closed until 9pm tonight. item.title: Man charged in relation to Co Monaghan fatal collision
item.description: Gardaí continue to investigate a fatal road traffic collision involving a HGV and a car on the N2 at Castleblayney, Co. Monaghan on Thursday, 18th December 2025. The road remains closed at this time while efforts are ongoing to safely remove the obstructing vehicle. The man in his 50s arrested in connection with this collision has since been charged and is due to appear before a special sitting of Monaghan District Court at 7:00pm this evening. Advertisement

item.title: Allianz to remain as GAA sponsor
item.description: The GAA has decided to continue their sponsorship relationship with Allianz. Allianz have been long term sponsors of the national football and hurling leagues. A number of county boards including Roscommon and Leitrim moved proposals to central council to remove Allianz as a sponsor. item.title: Man appears in court over death of woman in collision on the N2
item.description: A 56-year-old man has appeared in court tonight charged in relation to the death of Emma Mackeral. Ion Buccurica appeared at Monaghan District Court charged with dangerous driving causing the death of the Co Monaghan mother of two. The Romanian national who resides in France appeared in front of Judge Gerard Jones at a special sitting of Monaghan District Court over the alleged offence. Advertisement Inspector Damien Martin gave evidence of arrest, charge and caution at the brief hearing tonight
